claims.text: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC alloy with excellent high-temperature mechanical properties and poor room-temperature ductility.
High-temperature solutionizing can homogenize NbMoTaW into a single-phase BCC state.
Moderate-temperature annealing for an extended period followed by rapid cooling can form discrete B2 nanoprecipitates in NbMoTaW.
The resulting B2 nanoprecipitates will be coherent with the continuous BCC matrix.
An inverted microstructure consisting of discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix can improve room-temperature ductility.
An inverted BCC-matrix/B2-precipitate microstructure can maintain high yield strength at room and elevated temperatures.
Continuous ordered B2 matrices are associated with poor room-temperature ductility in two-phase refractory high-entropy alloys.
Discrete B2 precipitates impede dislocation motion in a controlled manner.
Controlled impediment of dislocation motion by B2 precipitates enhances strain hardening and room-temperature ductility.
The coherence and fine distribution of B2 precipitates preserve high-temperature yield strength.
B2 nanoprecipitates provide defect sinks that help maintain irradiation resistance.
Treated NbMoTaW will exhibit greater room-temperature plastic strain before fracture than untreated single-phase NbMoTaW.
Treated NbMoTaW will retain its yield strength at 1600 °C without a significant loss relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
Treated NbMoTaW will retain irradiation resistance relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
Overly aggressive annealing can coarsen the precipitates or produce continuous brittle phases.
Precipitate coarsening or continuous brittle-phase formation would negate the ductility benefit and could impair high-temperature or irradiation performance.
